hook: Planning season isn't about picking tactics. It's about deciding what you actually believe your organization can do.
direction: Angle: most orgs open a blank planning doc and immediately jump to channels and budgets — skipping the conviction layer that makes any plan hold. Cover: why strategy without belief collapses under pressure; why mission-driven orgs have an advantage here if they use it. Graphic: quote card — pull the core conviction as a bold centered statement.

facebook.text:
Planning season isn't about picking tactics. It's about deciding what you actually believe your organization can do.

Most teams open a blank doc and go straight to channels, budgets, and posting schedules. They skip the harder question: do we actually believe this mission is worth the effort we're about to plan?

That skipped layer is why so many plans fall apart by February. Pressure hits, and there's nothing underneath to hold.

Mission-driven organizations have a real advantage here, if they use it. You already have a reason that runs deeper than revenue. Build the plan from that, and the tactics have something to stand on.

instagram.text:
Planning season isn't about picking tactics. It's about deciding what you actually believe your organization can do.

Most teams skip straight to channels and budgets. They never ask the harder question underneath: do we believe this is worth it?

That's the layer that holds a plan together when things get hard. Without it, even a well-built strategy collapses under pressure.

Mission-driven organizations already have the answer. The work is building the plan from that conviction outward, not bolting it on at the end.

data.quote: A plan without conviction is just a schedule. Decide what you believe first.
